title: Chart Selection & Ethics
prompt: Choose the best chart type and identify misleading practices.
hints: Continuous time -> line chart; bar charts encode length from 0.
solution: Q1: Line chart; Q2: Truncating bar-chart y-axis
explanation: Line charts show trends over time, and bar charts require a zero baseline.

questions.question: Which chart best displays monthly revenue over 24 months?
questions.explanation: Line charts highlight continuity and trends across time.

questions.question: Why is starting a bar chart's y-axis at 95 instead of 0 misleading?
options: It makes a 2% difference look like a 200% difference in bar height
questions.explanation: Bar charts encode magnitude via bar length from zero.

title: Build a Labeled Matplotlib Bar Chart
prompt: Using matplotlib.pyplot as plt, create fig, ax = plt.subplots(), plot bars for ['Q1', 'Q2'] with values [100, 140], and set title to 'Quarterly Sales'.
solution:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

fig, ax = plt.subplots()
ax.bar(['Q1', 'Q2'], [100, 140])
ax.set_title('Quarterly Sales')
alternates:
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure()
plt.bar(['Q1', 'Q2'], [100, 140])
plt.title('Quarterly Sales')
fig = plt.gcf()
ax = plt.gca()
explanation: fig, ax = plt.subplots() gives direct control over bars, titles, and axis labels.

title: Bar chart baseline rule
prompt: Recall the y-axis rule for bar charts.
solution: Start the y-axis at 0 so bar lengths are proportional to values.
front: Why should bar charts almost always start their value axis at 0?
back: Because readers judge bar length proportionally; a non-zero baseline exaggerates small differences.
